newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Bearish on Taiwan mogas award.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Bearish on Taiwan mogas award.

text.p: The gasoline market was bearish on Thursday after Taiwan's purchase of only one cargo in its buy tender at low prices, traders said.
"It is pretty aggressive," a trader said on the price. "It suggests the market is seen as bearish."

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) said it bought one 250,000-barrel cargo of unleaded 95-octane reformate at around $24.70 per barrel c-and-f Keelung or Taichung arriving July 16-30 in a tender which closed on Wednesday.
"We are quite pleased with the price," a company official said. "It is in line if not lower than the Singapore market."
The award is lower than CPC's last tender award of two cargoes of unleaded reformate at $25.20 per barrel c-and-f for June 21-30 arrival and $24.92 for July 1-15 delivery.
"Mogas looks very weak if you look at the Taiwan numbers," a trader said.
The volume purchased was also below market expectations.
"We needed to take only one cargo," the official said, denying market rumours of a purchase of two cargoes.
Traders were now focused on results from India's gasoline tender for 25,000-tonnes of 87-octane leaded gasoline for delivery June 18-22 which is due on Friday.
Meanwhile, low Asian gasoline prices were pushing Mideast cargoes West while one trader and a national oil company were looking for June 95-octane supplies.
Bids for unleaded 95-octane c-and-f Mideast were heard at $3.50-$3.60 per barrel over Singapore naphtha spot quotes.
As a result and in the absence of fixed price talk on the Singapore fob markek, the grade was assessed $2.50 higher than Singapore naphtha swaps levels.
Naphtha June swaps were marginally firmer at $21.10/$21.30 per barrel and July at $21.45/$21.60.
Talk on the physical was thin with an early July cargo rumoured sold at 60-70 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes.
Sources close to Saudi Aramco said it was offering spot cargoes of A-180 and Jubail lifting June-September but not as much as 400,000-tonnes talked in the market.

Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) is likely to stick to its offer of $22.50 per tonne over the ADNOC formula for one-year term supplies of 500,000-700,000 tonnes of naphtha starting in July, traders said.
ADNOC is soon expected to notify Asian buyers of its counter offer to their bids at $19-$20 premiums.
